finding.claim: decode(subject=...) does not enforce the expected subject when the token has no sub claim, so a validly signed subject-less token is accepted for a subject-bound check.
finding.source: Attacker holds a token signed by the app's key that omits the sub claim (e.g. issued for another purpose by the same key).
finding.sink: Subject authorization check in _validate_sub, which is meant to accept only tokens whose sub equals the configured subject.

trace.note: decode_complete forwards subject to the claim validator
_validate_claims called after signature verification
verify_sub gate calls _validate_sub
returns early when 'sub' not in payload, skipping the subject comparison at 452-454

finding.guards_checked: Signature verified first (api_jws.py:277-285); verify_sub defaults True (api_jwt.py:61); non-string sub rejected (449-450). Missing sub is not rejected, unlike aud (529-532) and iss (571-572).

finding.claim: Short HMAC secrets are accepted by default: key-length enforcement is off and only a warning is emitted, so an attacker holding one token can brute-force the secret and forge tokens.
finding.source: Attacker holds a token signed with HS256/384/512 using a short or low-entropy app secret.
finding.sink: HMAC verification of arbitrary attacker-supplied tokens once the secret is recovered.

trace.note: _verify_signature calls check_key_length
HMACAlgorithm.check_key_length returns a message for keys below digest size
emits InsecureKeyLengthWarning and continues unless enforce_minimum_key_length
enforce_minimum_key_length defaults to False

finding.guards_checked: Empty-key and asymmetric/JWK-looking key checks (algorithms.py:346-440) do not address weak secrets. Default enforce_minimum_key_length=False (api_jwt.py:64, api_jws.py:60).

finding.claim: With cache_keys=True, signing keys are cached in an LRU with no time expiry, so a key removed from the JWKS (revoked or compromised) continues to verify tokens until evicted by size.
finding.source: Attacker holds a token signed by a key that was removed from the JWKS after compromise or rotation.
finding.sink: Signature verification using the cached PyJWK object, which is not re-checked against the JWKS.

trace.note: get_signing_key wrapped in lru_cache(maxsize=max_cached_keys)
get_signing_key returns cached PyJWK on hit
_verify_signature uses the PyJWK's key directly, with no JWKS re-check

finding.guards_checked: Documented in the docstring (jwks_client.py:69-72) and opt-in (default cache_keys=False). Eviction is size-only, max 16 entries.

finding.claim: ECDSA verification accepts high-S signatures, so a valid token has a second valid string form (s replaced by n-s), which defeats raw-token-string deny lists or replay caches.
finding.source: Attacker holds a valid ES256/384/512 token and computes s' = n - s.
finding.sink: Any revocation, deny-list or one-time-use check keyed on the raw token string or signature bytes.

trace.note: _verify_signature calls alg_obj.verify
ECAlgorithm.verify
raw_to_der_signature re-encodes r,s without a range check
public_key.verify accepts either s value

finding.guards_checked: Base64url canonicality enforced (api_jws.py:338), so only signature bytes vary. Curve check (algorithms.py:716-725) is unrelated. No low-S enforcement in the library.

finding.claim: When the app omits issuer=, the iss claim is not checked at all, so tokens minted for another issuer sharing the same key are accepted.
finding.source: Attacker holds a validly signed token from another service that uses the same key and includes an iss claim.
finding.sink: Application authorization that relies on decode() to bind tokens to one issuer.

trace.note: verify_iss gate calls _validate_iss
returns when issuer is None, so any iss passes

finding.guards_checked: Signature verified first. aud, by contrast, rejects a token carrying aud when the app passes no audience (api_jwt.py:522-527); iss has no equivalent guard.

finding.claim: Tokens lacking an exp claim are accepted indefinitely by default, because expiry is checked only when exp is present and require defaults to empty.
finding.source: Attacker holds a validly signed token issued without exp.

trace.note: exp check runs only if 'exp' in payload
require defaults to []

finding.guards_checked: Signature verified first. Expiry required only if the app sets require=['exp']. Consistent with RFC 7519 optionality.

finding.claim: Unknown-kid tokens trigger JWKS refetches with no backoff after a failed fetch, and the client lock is held during network I/O, so unauthenticated traffic can amplify outbound requests and serialize verification during a JWKS outage.
finding.source: Unauthenticated attacker sends tokens with unknown kid values, read via get_signing_key_from_jwt without signature verification.
finding.sink: Outbound HTTP to the JWKS endpoint under _client_lock with a default 30 s timeout.

trace.note: get_signing_key_from_jwt reads kid from unverified header
get_signing_key holds _client_lock during fetch
refresh path fetches on unknown kid when not cooling down
failed fetch does not update _last_successful_fetch, so no cooldown after failure

finding.guards_checked: 30 s cooldown after a successful fetch when cache_jwk_set=True (jwks_client.py:250-256). Cooldown is bypassed by design when cache_jwk_set=False (docstring :66-67).

finding.claim: If the app passes algorithms as a string rather than a list, alg membership becomes substring matching, letting an attacker-chosen registered algorithm name that is a substring of the configured string pass the allow-list.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled alg header value; developer misconfiguration passing a str for algorithms.
finding.sink: Algorithm allow-list check that selects the verification algorithm.

trace.note: decode_complete only checks algorithms is truthy
alg not in algorithms performs substring check on a str
get_algorithm_by_name selects the algorithm for the substring-matched alg

finding.guards_checked: EC curve check (algorithms.py:716-725) blocks ES256 vs secp256k1 key mismatch when the key is secp256k1; PEM/DER/SSH checks block HMAC with asymmetric keys; PyJWK alg must equal key.algorithm_name (api_jws.py:411). Exploitable only with developer misuse and a mismatched key type.

finding.claim: Claim validators catch only ValueError around int() conversion, so an exp/nbf/iat of Infinity (accepted by json.loads) or null raises OverflowError or TypeError out of decode() instead of a clean InvalidTokenError.
finding.source: A key-holder-signed token with exp Infinity or null, or an attacker payload if verify_signature is disabled.
finding.sink: Uncaught exception in the decode path.

trace.note: _validate_iat catches only ValueError around int(payload['iat'])
_validate_nbf same pattern
_validate_exp same pattern

finding.guards_checked: Signature verified first for normal decode, so the attacker must hold a signing key. Impact is an uncaught exception, not an auth bypass.
